children: New Delhi, Oct. 1 -- The managing director and CEO of HDFC Bank was paid Rs.15.13 crore for the financial year that ended March 2026, as per their annual report.

During the time, HDFC Bank's CEO and MD was Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is now set to vacate his position on 26 October. In August, the private lender had informed the Reserve Bank of India that Jagdishan had decided to not seek reappointment after the end of his term.

In the previous fiscal year, Jagdishan's basic pay was Rs.3.09 crore and his allowances totaled Rs.3.46 crore. Jagdishan was paid a 35 per cent performance bonus, which climbed from Rs.4.67 crore in FY25 to Rs.7.28 crore in FY26.
His employee stock option plan (ESOP) holdings more than doubled, rising from 2.12 lakh to 4.28 lakh shares.
In accordance to guidelines issued by the RBI, he also received a 50 per cent cash variable pay component worth Rs.2.67 crore for his performance in 2024-25, which disbursed in January 2026.
With Jagdishan set to vacate his position on 26 October, he is set to be replaced by Anup Bagchi, the ICICI veteran. The RBI approved Bagchi as the new CEO and MD of HDFC Bank on Thursday.

The resignation of Jagdishan came months after Chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned in March, saying certain practices at the bank were at odds with his "personal values and ethics". An independent legal review later found no evidence to substantiate Chakraborty's governance-related concerns.
Executive Director and Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Maneck Bharucha took home Rs.17.14 crore in the last fiscal, outpacing the earnings of the MD and CEO.

Elevated to whole-time director in January, Bharucha drew a basic salary of Rs.3.59 crore. His performance bonus jumped a 100 per cent to Rs.8.59 crore, up from Rs.4.19 crore last year. His ESOP grants also jumped five times, surging to 6.23 lakh from 1.30 lakh shares.

A veteran of ICICI for 24 years, Anup Bagchi will now be heading HDFC Bank. His appointment marks the first time an external candidate will lead HDFC Bank. The lender had previously been headed by banking veteran Aditya Puri for 25 years before Jagdishan succeeded him in 2020.
